edges.label: contracting at a site whose existence was itself classified
edges.note: EG&G instrumented and fired US nuclear tests from the Manhattan Project onward and became the classified services contractor for the Nevada complex, including the Air Force operating location near Groom Lake - a facility whose existence required a Presidential Determination published at 60 FR 52823 to exempt it from disclosure. It is the historical template for how contracting works where the place of performance cannot be named.

edges.label: EG&G provided the classified site services and personnel transport for the Groom Lake operating location
edges.note: The relationship is documented indirectly through the Groom Lake worker litigation and the annual presidential environmental exemptions rather than through any acknowledgment of the facility.

a.label: Presidential Determinations on the Air Force's Operating Location Near Groom Lake

edges.label: The state secrets defence shielded the contractor-operated facility from the workers' suit
edges.note: Rather than litigate the alleged open-air burning of classified waste, the government invoked state secrets and the President exempted the site; Kasza v. Browner, 133 F.3d 1159, sustained dismissal and certiorari was denied.

a.label: Presidential Determinations on the Air Force's Operating Location Near Groom Lake

edges.label: Annual presidential determinations exempt the Groom Lake operating location from environmental disclosure
edges.note: Published in the Federal Register every year since 1995, the determinations never name the facility or describe its contents - the cleanest documentary proof of a contractor-operated site legally exempted from statutory disclosure.
